title: U.S. House · Texas's 9th District
area: A redrawn district covering the Houston Ship Channel area and Liberty County, east and southeast of Houston.

context.text: Open seat. Texas redrew its congressional map in August 2025, and the redrawn 9th District became substantially more Republican-leaning than the district previously represented by Democratic incumbent Al Green. Rather than run for re-election here, Green ran against fellow Democratic incumbent Christian Menefee in the redrawn, safely Democratic 18th District, and lost the May 26, 2026 primary runoff. Leticia Gutierrez won the Democratic primary for the open 9th District seat; Alex Mealer won a Republican primary runoff over Briscoe Cain.

candidates.name: Leticia Gutierrez
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary in a multi-candidate field

summary.text: Leticia Gutierrez is the Democratic nominee for the open U.S. House seat in Texas's 9th District. She holds a finance and economics degree from the University of St. Thomas and has focused her campaign on affordability and infrastructure resilience following the district's history of hurricanes and winter storms.

background.text: Holds a degree in Finance and Economics from the University of St. Thomas.

priorities.text: Everyday affordability: says rising costs of groceries and other necessities are forcing families to forgo healthcare and housing investments.
Making government work for constituents, including ending what she describes as subsidies to large corporations paid for by working families.
Infrastructure resilience: cites Hurricane Harvey, Winter Storm Uri and the 2024 derecho as reasons to invest in aging pipes, power lines and roads.

positions.summary: Says the government has been giving subsidies to large corporations while working families 'foot the bill,' and wants that to end.

candidates.name: Alex Mealer
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 26, 2026 Republican primary runoff over Briscoe Cain

summary.text: Alex Mealer is the Republican nominee for the open U.S. House seat in Texas's 9th District. A West Point graduate, Army combat veteran and Harvard-trained lawyer, she worked in energy-sector finance before running for Congress on a platform built around border security, public safety and the Houston Ship Channel economy.

background.text: Graduated from the United States Military Academy at West Point and served as an Explosive Ordnance Disposal officer in the U.S. Army, including combat deployment to Afghanistan.

Earned an MBA from Harvard Business School and a law degree from Harvard Law School, then worked in Houston advising energy companies on mergers, acquisitions and capital-markets transactions before becoming a small-business owner.

priorities.text: Border security and immigration enforcement, framed as part of a broader 'America First' agenda.
Public safety: says law enforcement should be fully resourced and equipped to protect communities.
Protecting the Houston Ship Channel and port economy, which she says generates more than $1 trillion in GDP for the region.

positions.summary: Lists keeping the border secure as the first item of her platform to pass what she calls President Trump's 'America First Agenda.'
Says she is committed to ensuring law enforcement is 'fully resourced' with the tools needed to protect communities.
